answer: Sybil farms fail when admission is a scarce watering right, not a free key. A newcomer reserves one numbered stall at a public oasis; the stall issues a single non-transferable willow token bound to a live device check. Each epoch that token authorizes one beacon-seeded chore in a short window, and the signed receipt is lashed to the next vacant rung of a published trellis so work cannot be backdated or batched. If two names share a stall, a token serial, or a chore transcript, both deposits burn and the stall stays dark for twelve epochs. Farms then exhaust stalls and tokens, not ballots.
